text:
The board is the feature herddash is measured by: a notification center with one box per agent showing status, owning account and time waiting, sorted longest-waiting first; read-only, no terminal, no chat, no pane control. The recorder engine (subscribe, persist transitions, attribute, read-only API, event stream) is what makes the board trustworthy and feeds future surfaces. Corrects ADR-0001's consequence that the board is secondary; to be recorded as ADR-0003.

Why: The operator's daily value is glancing at the board in another window all day; a PRD that calls it secondary would produce epics that treat it as secondary, the success metric (noticing a waiting agent sooner than the toast) is a board metric, and the differentiator the operator believes in is restraint, a notification center rather than a browser client, which can only be defended if the board is the product being restrained.

Epoch rule (spine AD-3, Story 1.6): on the first snapshot after every reconnect, keep the server epoch only if at least one tracked pane is present with the same non-empty terminal_id; otherwise increment it, removing every tracked Agent under the old epoch. Within a kept epoch, a pane whose pane id survives but whose terminal_id changed is a new Agent, never joined. A pane-id match alone never keeps an epoch. The epoch lives in memory until milestone 2 persists it with the pane-to-terminal_id map (hazard 3 open).

Why: Story 1.3 found herdr names no server instance; a new one shows as a new terminal_id per pane (observed ids look time-derived, e.g. term_65df2e06a79ca1 → term_65df2e18d44a41, not counters), and a fresh server reissues pane ids from w1:p1. Agents do not survive a non-handoff herdr restart (restored panes run fresh shells), so incrementing on a new instance is truthful. Effect of server.live_handoff on terminal_id is untested.

Story 1.7 resync design (spec-1-7): resync is a named engine operation triggered by any status-stream health signal, a rejected/failed status subscribe, or a snapshot showing a tracked Agent without a subscription. One resync runs at a time, a trigger during one causes exactly one more, and resyncs start at least resyncMinInterval (default 5 s) apart. Each resync is announced via Sink.Resynced(cause) as it begins, resubscribes unsubscribed panes, and ends when a snapshot read started after those subscribes settled has been applied. apply() subscribes only newly tracked panes, which bounds the rejection loop deferred from Story 1.5. A reconcile timer requests a snapshot every reconcileInterval (default 60 s). Lifecycle-stream signals keep Story 1.6's reconnect, whose Reconnected report is the marker.

Why: AD-11 requires a single resync guard and minimum interval in the engine, and FR-7 requires every gap to be announced. Funnelling the per-pane recovery paths through one guarded operation serialises a lost-events condition that drops many pane connections, and makes the persistent-rejection loop cost one subscribe per interval. The lifecycle stream already has a reconnect that resubscribes, snapshots and replaces state.

Story 1.8 version gate (spec-1-8): core.DecideGate(version, allowUnsupported) is pure core. It parses MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH from ping's version string (leading v, -/+ suffix ignored); an empty or unparsable version counts as below the minimum. The gate is decided after ping and before the lifecycle subscribe. Refused: no subscription or snapshot, every tracked Agent removed ("herdr refused"), re-pinged every refusedRecheckInterval (30 s) outside the reconnect backoff. Advisory: observed normally, with a warning per connect that adds "resync guarantee does not hold below 0.9.0" below 0.9.0. Sink.Gate is reported only when the outcome or version changes. serve prints a gate line and herdr=<v> on transition lines. Epoch state survives a refusal, so an upgrade goes through the AD-3 epoch rule.

Why: FR-16 and ADR-0006 require refusing below 0.9.5 unless the dogfooding flag is set. Gating before the subscribe means a refused server is truly observed by nothing. Re-pinging on a fixed timer notices the operator's 0.8.2 server being restarted as 0.9.5 without hammering it. ConnectionTruth and the Board strip are Epic 3, so the Sink report is the Epic 1 surface.

text: macOS omits the environment from kern.procargs2 for Apple-signed binaries (e.g. /bin/sleep) when the caller is not root: only exec path and argv come back. herddash's procenv treats a buffer with no environment entries as ErrNoEnvironment, so the Profile is `unresolved` rather than the rule's absent case. Claude Code's binary is signed by Anthropic (Identifier com.anthropic.claude-code, TeamIdentifier Q6L2SF6YDW, checked 2026-10-19), so its environment is readable. Tests that need a readable child environment on darwin must spawn a non-Apple binary, e.g. the test binary re-executed (TestHelperSleep in cmd/herddash/serve_test.go).
